t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in coordination with the heads of other departments and agencies, shall, as appropriate, through existing programs and activities, advance the education and awareness of the public (including providers, patients, and consumers) and other appropriate entities regarding the risk of abuse of prescription opioids if such drugs are not taken as prescribed. 
    (b) Topics.—The education and awareness campaigns under subsection (a) shall address—
        (1) the dangers of opioid abuse; 
        (2) the prevention of opioid abuse, including through safe disposal of prescription medications and other safety precautions; and 
        (3) the detection of early warning signs of addiction.  
    (c) Other Requirements.—The education and awareness campaigns under subsection (a) shall, as appropriate—
        (1) take into account any association between prescription opioid abuse and heroin use; 
        (2) emphasize—
            (A) the similarities between heroin and prescription opioids; and 
            (B) the effects of heroin and prescription opioids on the human body; and  
        (3) bring greater public awareness to the dangerous effects of fentanyl when mixed with heroin or abused in a similar manner.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "coordination" and the references to the public, providers, patients and consumers signal participation. But the coordination is only with heads of other federal departments and agencies, which is intra-government. The public is merely the audience of a one-way education and awareness campaign, not a party consulted before a federal decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in coordination with the heads of other departments and agencies, shall, as appropriate, through existing programs and activities, advance the education and awareness of the public

opus.w: The only coordination here is between the HHS Secretary and the heads of other federal departments and agencies. All of them are inside the federal government. The section also mentions "the public" and "providers, patients, and consumers," but only as the people who receive education campaigns. That is one-way communication from the government, so these groups are not consulted on any federal decision and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in coordination with the heads of other departments and agencies, shall, as appropriate, through existing programs and activities, advance the education and awareness of the public

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the government to educate the public about opioid risks. It does not require the government to consult with the public, states, or other outside entities before making a decision. The coordination mentioned is between federal agencies ('heads of other departments and agencies'), which is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. The public is the target of the outreach, not a participant in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in coordination with the heads of other departments and agencies, shall, as appropriate, through existing programs and activities, advance the education and awareness of the public (including providers, patients, and consumers) and other appropriate entities regarding the risk of abuse of prescription opioids if such drugs are not taken as prescribed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "advancing the education and awareness of the public" constitutes participation because it involves the public. However, participation requires the government to *consult* or *coordinate with* outside parties *before* making a decision, or to grant them a role in the decision-making process (e.g., via an advisory board or comment period). Here, the government is simply disseminating information *to* the public. The public is the recipient of the action, not a participant in the decision-making process. There is no requirement for the public to provide input, advice, or feedback that influences the government's actions.
